Compute 2Φ(−Φ⁻¹(.975)√6); the independent evaluation gives 1.57944924024×10⁻⁶. correctness.rationale: For the specified fully known uniform null, the n+1 complete spacings have the Dirichlet(1,…,1) law. The statistic gives both endpoint weights zero. The diagonal term is nB_n and the ordered off-diagonal sum subtracts A_n²−B_n over the same denominator (n+1)²(n+2), giving the claimed correction. All interior weights are positive, so the gap is zero at n=2 and strictly positive from n=3. The profile integrals are m=1/[2(θ+1)] and b=2/[3(θ+2)(2θ+1)]; the exact variance times n tends to b−m²>0. For the fixed-order CLT, represent the spacings by independent unit exponentials divided by their sum, and center each coefficient by A_n/(n+1). The centered coefficients sum to zero and are uniformly bounded, their squared sum divided by n tends to b−m², and the third absolute moments give a Lyapunov ratio O(n^(−1/2)); the exponential sum divided by n tends to one. This proves the CLT and, comparing to the stated printed formula, gives b/(b−m²). The difference identities against 4 and 32/5 verify strict bounds and their sharp limiting orders. The exact-mean-centered two-sided normal rule rejects asymptotically at the claimed Gaussian tail, not nominal size. Independent rational power-sum checks for n=2,…,300 at θ=2 and the standard-normal tail reproduce the example and cutoffs. This decision verifies the theorem for the written statistic and variance; the correspondence with the cited article is supported by the frozen equation locators and matching numerical benchmark but not by independently inspected primary equations or Table 1.
residual_risks: Original equation and Table 1 transcriptions not directly verified; the frozen source reports Table 1 Monte Carlo cutoffs [0.1497,0.1792]. Fixed θ, a fully specified uniform null, and the explicit exact-mean/printed-variance normal rule only; no claim about corrected, simulated or composite-null calibration.

value.rationale: A correction to an actual proposed inferential calibration is worthwhile when the distortion materially changes the conclusions. The result gives the sharp size distortion profile across all fixed permitted entropy orders, attributes it to omitted spacing correlations, and shows that a nominal 5% rule can have asymptotic size about 0.000158% at θ=2. That is substantively more than displaying the standard covariance identity, while making no claim against simulation-calibrated implementations.
residual_risks: Practical consequence is conditional on using the stated printed-variance normal formula, not on all instances of the CRTE test; power and moving-order behavior not addressed.
